“And show you compassion, … and have compassion upon you,

p: Rav Natan bar Abba said … Rav said:
Rav Natan bar Abba said that Rav said:
Whoever looks to the table of others
the world is dark for him. … for it is stated: … “He wanders abroad for bread: … Where is it?
the world is dark for him. Everything looks bleak and hopeless to him, for it is stated: “He wanders abroad for bread: Where is it?
He knows the day of darkness is ready at his hand”
Even his life is no life,
and they are as follows: … One who looks to the table of others
and they are as follows: One who looks to the table of others
and one whose body is ruled by suffering.
Even one who has only one robe.

p: Rav Aḥa from Hutzal said to us that the master, … to plaster
Rav Aḥa from Hutzal said to us that the master, Rav Ashi, allows his attendants to plaster
the oven for him on a Festival.
We rely on the bank of the Euphrates … And this applies only when one wrapped
We rely on the bank of the Euphrates River. We avoid the labor of kneading by taking sufficiently kneaded mud from the riverbank. The Gemara comments: And this applies only when one wrapped

p: One may not draw two barrels together
it is permitted to put them together
Rabba raised an objection to Rav Naḥman:
one may not draw two barrels together
to place a pot on them?
He said to him: … There, … it is different,
He said to him: There, with regard to barrels, it is different,
on a Festival, … one built … bench [itztaba],
on a Festival, one built a solid bench [itztaba],
one does not make a tent,
the Torah prohibited … a permanent construction, … the Torah did not prohibit … a temporary construction.
the Torah prohibited erecting a permanent construction, but the Torah did not prohibit erecting a temporary construction.
the Sages did not decree with regard to it.
